results.reason: The memo identifies the asymmetric assignment in SA §13.2 and notes Supplier can assign to a competitor without notice. It also proposes a competitor carve-out. But its 'why it matters' discussion is about change-of-control hold-up. It never explains the supply-continuity or confidential-specification risk of a Supplier assignment.

The memo identifies that §13.3 requires Supplier consent for a change of control and gives Supplier a termination right. It explains the veto/hold-up risk over any sale or merger. It recommends deletion, or limiting the clause to competitor acquirers with notice. It does not know of the pending sale, but it covers sale scenarios and asks the client about corporate plans.
The memo identifies OF §2.2's three-year auto-renewal with a 30-day notice window and explains the lock-in risk. It recommends no auto-renewal, or one-year renewals with 90-day notice.
The memo notes that §9.3 leaves Customer's indemnity uncapped while Supplier's is capped. It recommends replacing §9.3 with a mutual carve-out and narrowing the Customer indemnity.
The memo correctly states the cap as fees paid in the prior 12 months (§9.1), the three-year term from March 1, 2026, and Delaware law.
The memo correctly applies SA > OF > Spec precedence, including noting that the OF renewal clause conflicts with SA §2.1 and that the SA governs.
The memo uses a tiered structure. The indemnity/cap issue (Issue 2) and change of control (Issue 3) are both in Tier 1, ahead of lesser issues.
Each issue is structured with location, problem/why it matters, and a fix with proposed language. A closing section lists client input and business decisions needed.
The memo flags the Specifications Schedule as problematic (Issue 1 mismatch, Issue 13 spec gaps). It also cites UCC § 2-316 / 6 Del. C. § 2-316, which is outside authority not found in the documents.
